subject: Urgent: model v13-alpha latency spike — request for controlled rollback & routing cap
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@solstice.ai>, ops@solstice.ai
Date: 2025-11-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] model v13-alpha p95 spike starting 09:05 PT

Team —

Monitoring alerted at ~09:05 PT: p95 for text-generation routes running model v13-alpha jumped from ~210ms to ~1.8s across several shards. Error rates are stable, but tail latency is elevated for both hosted and Dedicated traffic. Spike coincides with a canary that was promoted at 08:58 PT (v13-alpha 2025-11-12-0858).

Initial observations: 
- Affected routes: /v1/generate (customer routes using v13-alpha).
- Percent of total traffic hitting v13-alpha: ~18% (canary promotion pushed ~12% internal + 6% prod).
- P95 increase: ~210ms -> 1800ms; p99 also elevated.
- No kernel OOMs; GPUs show modest UTIL increase.

I’ve opened INC-20251112-87 and attached a p95 snapshot and traffic heatmap. Asking for:
1) Product/Sales: notify impacted customers and propose a mitigation (traffic cap or temporary rollback).
2) Eng: evaluate quick rollback plan and risk (can we safely revert to v12-stable for affected variants?).
3) CS: confirm customer impact and appetite for a staged rollback.

I recommend we limit external-facing traffic to <10% on v13-alpha while we triage, or rollback if the customer prefers.

-Ethan

--
Ethan Park
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@solstice.ai>, ops@solstice.ai
Date: 2025-11-12T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] model v13-alpha p95 spike starting 09:05 PT

Thanks Ethan. Appreciate the quick detection. Rafael here from Support/Account.

Grace / Mina — can we get a short recommendation on two options: (A) controlled rollback of customer traffic from v13-alpha -> v12-stable for Solstice; (B) apply a routing cap (10%) + automated fallback to v12 on per-request timeouts while we investigate root cause?

If option A is safe, I’ll request authorization for a targeted rollback for Solstice only. If we need Exec-level sign-off for an account-specific rollback, flag here so I can escalate to Sales Ops. Carolyn — I’ll keep you posted; please confirm whether Solstice wants a rollback or prefers a temporary routing cap.

Rafael
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@solstice.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@solstice.ai
Date: 2025-11-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] model v13-alpha p95 spike starting 09:05 PT

Thanks for the heads up. Impact on Solstice: our ingestion pipeline is timing out on some user requests (roughly 7% of requests in the last 30 minutes). Business impact is moderate — some UI calls are degraded but no data loss.

We prefer a rollback for now (option A) limited to Solstice traffic only; please avoid a global rollback. If rollback will take longer than 20 minutes, we’d accept a temporary routing cap to 5% while you execute. Please confirm ETA and whether there will be any schema/semantics change that could affect our downstream parsing.

Carolyn Park
Platform Ops — Solstice AI
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@solstice.ai>, ops@solstice.ai
Date: 2025-11-12T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] model v13-alpha p95 spike starting 09:05 PT

Quick technical note and rollback plan (TL;DR: we can do a targeted rollback for Solstice only; low technical risk, short window).

What I checked:
- Canary logs: increased attention-memory pressure on specific sequence-length patterns introduced by v13-alpha attention fusion path. Not OOM; latency increases due to suboptimal kernel selection at ~512-1024 token lengths in some micro-batches.
- Telemetry: KV cache hit rates unchanged; CPU overhead small.

Rollback plan (targeted to Solstice):
1) Route Solstice production routes from v13-alpha -> v12-stable (per-route override) at 12:25 PT.
2) Keep global canary at 12% internal for v13-alpha for further investigation.
3) Monitor p95/p99 for 15m; if stable, hold. If regressions persist, expand rollback.
4) Expected customer-visible downtime: ~30-90s while routing flips and caches warm.

Risks: slight inconsistency in inference outputs between v12 and v13 (semantic diffs are minor for Solstice’s use case, but we’ll flag any data drift). No schema changes.

Attachments: p95_spike_snapshot_20251112.png (attached), traffic_heatmap_11-12.csv (attached)

Authorization request: Rafael/Grace — please confirm authorization to execute the targeted route rollback now. Also request permission to apply a temporary per-route SLO tolerance of +500ms on Solstice for 2 hours to avoid automated incident escalation noise.

-Mina
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Carolyn Park <carolyn.park@solstice.ai>, ops@solstice.ai
Date: 2025-11-12T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] model v13-alpha p95 spike starting 09:05 PT

Authorization granted.

Approve targeted rollback for Solstice (route override v13-alpha -> v12-stable) with the following constraints:
- Limit scope to Solstice only. No global rollback.
- Apply routing flip at 15:50 PT; Mina to execute and confirm in thread when complete.
- Apply a temporary per-route SLO tolerance of +500ms for 2 hours; Engineering and SRE to mute automated pager escalation for this route for the window.
- Rafael: send customer note to Carolyn confirming ETA and expected ~60s transient latency at flip; offer follow-up post-mortem within 48 hours.

Thanks for moving quickly. Keep me posted if rollback uncovers regressions in v12 signals.

Tessa Morgan
Director, Sales Operations (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
